hooks.text: A minor planet barely 155 miles wide is wearing icy rings.
Rings were supposed to belong only to massive gas giants.
A 155-mile-wide rock shattered our rules about planetary rings.

title: The 155-Mile Asteroid with Its Own Rings
description: Astronomers assumed only colossal gas giants possessed dense rings. Then a tiny 155-mile-wide centaur proved them wrong.

beats.text: A minor planet barely 155 miles wide is wearing icy rings.
beats.visual: Artist's impression of asteroid Chariklo encircled by its two dense rings, 2014

beats.text: For centuries, rings were only confirmed around giant planets: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.
beats.visual: Cassini mosaic of Saturn showing its magnificent planetary ring system, 2004

beats.text: In 2013, Brazilian astronomer Felipe Braga-Ribas watched the centaur Chariklo pass in front of a star.
beats.visual: Danish 1.54-metre telescope dome at ESO's La Silla Observatory at night, 2013

beats.text: The starlight blinked briefly seconds before and after the rock passed, revealing two distinct rings.
beats.visual: Occultation light curve graph demonstrating starlight dips from Chariklo's rings, 2014

beats.text: Down from planetary scales, these rings orbit only about 400 kilometers from Chariklo's center.
beats.visual: Diagram showing the close orbit of Chariklo's rings around the centaur, 2014

beats.text: Even wilder, the two icy bands measure just seven kilometers and three kilometers wide.
beats.visual: Artist's concept detailing the two narrow icy rings Oiapoque and Chuí, 2014

beats.text: That solved an old mystery: Chariklo dimmed for a decade when its rings tilted edge-on to Earth.
beats.visual: Diagram illustrating Chariklo's rings tilting edge-on to Earth during orbit, 2014

beats.text: Astronomers hypothesize unseen shepherd moons keep them stable, preserving an impossible sight.
beats.visual: Artist's impression of a shepherd moon maintaining an icy ring system, 2014
queries: Shepherd moon asteroid ring artist concept

better_than_last: Applies the scale ladder framework by stepping down from giant gas planets directly to kilometer-scale ring measurements across beats 2 to 6, avoiding administrative lists to maintain narrative tension and secure a seamless audio loop.
